title: Affine shrinking and quasi-compact descent of an invariant section component
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ be a flat morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with geometrically reduced fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $p:Z\to B$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $\sigma:Z\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=p$. Put $Y=X\times_B Z$, let $s=(\sigma,\mathrm{id}_Z)$ be its section over $Z$, and define $C\subseteq Y$ as the union of the connected components of the fibres containing $s$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $C$ is open [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $R=Z\times_B Z$, with structure map $q:R\to B$, and write $a_i:X\times_B R\to Y$ and $h:X\times_B R\to R$ for the induced projections. Let $b_0\in B$ with $Z_{b_0}\ne\varnothing$. Suppose an open $W\subseteq R$ contains $q^{-1}(b_0)$ and satisfies $h^{-1}W\cap a_0^{-1}C=h^{-1}W\cap a_1^{-1}C$. Then there exist an affine open $V\subseteq B$ containing $b_0$ and a unique open $U\subseteq X_V=X\times_B V$ such that $q^{-1}V\subseteq W$, $p_V:Z_V\to V$ is finite locally free and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], $Z_V$ is affine, and $\pi^{-1}U=C_V$ for $\pi:X_V\times_V Z_V\to X_V$ and $C_V=C\times_B V$. Both $p_V$ and $\pi$ are fpqc coverings [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], and both $C_V$ and $U$ are quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Uniqueness is for the chosen $V$ and its specified pullback $C_V$. No geometric connectedness of $X_{b_0}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof from finite locally free open-and-closed shrinking through fpqc descent and the final quasi-compactness paragraph.

proof.text: By the definition of finite locally free, $p$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. The first projection $R=Z\times_B Z\to Z$ is finite by base change, hence its composite $q:R\to B$ is finite. Therefore $D=q(R\setminus W)$ is closed in $B$. Since $q^{-1}(b_0)\subseteq W$, $b_0\notin D$. Also $p$ is open because it is flat and locally of finite presentation, so $p(Z)$ is an open neighbourhood of $b_0$ (the fibre is nonempty). Choose an affine open $b_0\in V\subseteq p(Z)\setminus D$. Then $q^{-1}V\subseteq W$ and every point of $V$ has a preimage under $p$.

proof.text: Base change preserves finiteness, flatness, and local finite presentation, so p_V is finite locally free. The pullback-point range formula and V ⊆ range(p) prove surjectivity of p_V; finiteness over affine V gives an affine source Z_V. The projection π is finite, flat, and surjective by base change of the corresponding individual morphism properties. Apply Scheme.Hom.singleton_mem_fpqcPrecoverage to p_V and π. This verifies both singleton coverings directly rather than invoking base change of a covering family.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, affine shrinking and descent paragraphs

proof.text: Put P = X_V ×_V Z_V, π:P→X_V, and ρ:P→Z_V. On Q=P×_{X_V}P, let l,r be the projections. Their composites to X_V agree, so the two maps Q→Z obtained from ρ give a map d:Q→Z×_B Z. Together with the common map Q→X this gives e:Q→X×_B(Z×_B Z). Pullback extensionality proves e composed with a_0 and a_1 equals l and r composed with restrictionMap. Its map to B factors through V, so q^{-1}(V)⊆W puts e(Q) inside h^{-1}(W). Evaluating the supplied invariance equality at e(x) gives equal pullbacks of C_V on Q. Apply openSubscheme_existsUnique_of_fpqc to the PUnit-indexed singleton family π; obtain U and its uniqueness for the chosen V.

source.place: Tag 03N0, lemma-open-fpqc-covering; applied as in Tag 057I

proof.text: Let Y=X×_B Z with g:Y→Z, and let r_Z:Z_V→Z be the restriction projection. Pullback pasting and cancellation show that restrictionMap:P→Y, together with ρ:P→Z_V, is a cartesian square, hence gives an isomorphism e:P≅Y×_Z Z_V compatible with its first projection. Let s be the section of g induced by σ. The canonical base-change specialization of the section-component cartesian theorem (Stacks 055M; preimage_setOf_mem_connectedComponentIn_preimage_singleton in SlicingFlat) identifies the inverse image of C in Y×_Z Z_V with the relative component of the base-changed section. The base Z_V is affine; base change supplies local finite presentation and quasi-compact/quasi-separated morphisms, hence compact and quasi-separated total and base spaces. Apply isCompact_setOf_mem_connectedComponentIn_preimage_singleton to get compactness there. Pull this compact open back along e.hom, a quasi-compact isomorphism, to obtain compactness of C_V. The existing compactness theorem needs neither flatness nor geometrically reduced fibres, so no field-extension argument is necessary.

source.place: Tag 057I, final quasi-compactness paragraph, using Tag 055P (lemma-connected-along-section-locally-constructible) through the existing section-component quasi-compactness node

proof.text: From π^{-1}(U)=C_V and surjectivity of π obtain π(C_V)=U using Set.image_preimage_eq. The continuous image of the compact set C_V under π is compact, so U is compact. Combine the affine shrinking, finite locally free and surjective cover, two singleton fpqc membership proofs, compactness, descent equality, and uniqueness in the required conjunction. No hypothesis of geometric connectedness was used.

split_report.summary: Expanded the affine shrinking and fpqc descent tail of Stacks Tag 057I into five steps. Shrink simultaneously away from the finite image of R minus W and into the open image of p. Verify finite locally free, affine and fpqc properties before invoking open descent; reuse the existing section-component quasi-compactness theorem, checking its affine-base and geometrically reduced fibre hypotheses, then prove quasi-compactness downstairs by an open-cover argument. No new nodes or changes to the statement.

Step 2: p_V is finite locally free and surjective, and Z_V is affine. Step 3: P×_{X_V}P ≅ X×_B q^{-1}V ⊆ h^{-1}W, its projections are the restricted a_i, and the cited 03N0 node states both existence and uniqueness of U. Step 4: g is flat, finitely presented and qcqs; its fibres X_b⊗κ(z) are geometrically reduced; C_V is exactly the section-component set over Z_V; Z_V is affine. These are the hypotheses of lem-trf-section-component-quasi-compact (Lean-closed). Step 5 is elementary: π(C_V)=U by surjectivity, so U is quasi-compact as a continuous image. lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_open_invariant_component_descent {X Z B : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [GeometricallyReduced f] (p : Z ⟶ B) [p.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (σ : Z ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = p) (C : (pullback f p).Opens) (hC : C.carrier = {y | y ∈ connectedComponentIn ((pullback.snd f p) ⁻¹' {(pullback.snd f p) y}) ((pullback.lift σ (𝟙 Z) (hσ.trans (Category.id_comp p).symm)) ((pullback.snd f p) y))}) (b₀ : B) (hb₀ : Nonempty (p.fiber b₀)) (W : (pullback p p).Opens) (hW : (overlapBase p) ⁻¹' {b₀} ⊆ W.carrier) (hInv : ((pullback.snd f (overlapBase p)) ⁻¹ᵁ W) ⊓ ((overlapLeft f p) ⁻¹ᵁ C) = ((pullback.snd f (overlapBase p)) ⁻¹ᵁ W) ⊓ ((overlapRight f p) ⁻¹ᵁ C)) : ∃ V : B.Opens, b₀ ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ (overlapBase p) ⁻¹' (V : Set B) ⊆ W.carrier ∧ (pullback.snd p V.ι).IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ Surjective (pullback.snd p V.ι) ∧ IsAffine (pullback p V.ι) ∧ Presieve.singleton (pullback.snd p V.ι) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage V.toScheme ∧ Presieve.singleton (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f V.ι) (pullback.snd p V.ι)) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (pullback f V.ι) ∧ IsCompact ((restrictionMap f p V) ⁻¹' C.carrier) ∧ ∃ U : (pullback f V.ι).Opens, IsCompact U.carrier ∧ (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f V.ι) (pullback.snd p V.ι)) ⁻¹ᵁ U = (restrictionMap f p V) ⁻¹ᵁ C ∧ ∀ U' : (pullback f V.ι).Opens, (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f V.ι) (pullback.snd p V.ι)) ⁻¹ᵁ U' = (restrictionMap f p V) ⁻¹ᵁ C → U' = U
